Sample.evidence_source: The number of participants (N = 249) exceeded the minimum 5:1 participants-to-parameter ratio needed to confidently examine a model (Bentler, 1990). In this study, a total of 225 participants were needed as there were 45 parameters (25 variable-to-variable paths, 10 standard error paths to the model variables, five BMI-to-variable paths, and five BMI standard error paths) in Fig. 1. Our sample size also exceeded the N ">= 200 recommendation for complex models (Weston & Gore, 2006).

section_summary.extract_value: This section details the testing of a hypothesized model, starting with the justification of the sample size (N = 249) and the statistical methods used (Mplus, CFI, SRMR, RMSEA). It describes the examination of the initial structural model, the deletion of nonsignificant paths to create a trimmed model, and further revision based on modification indices. The final model, with significant standardized path coefficients, is presented, highlighting the variance accounted for in body appreciation, intuitive eating, depressive symptoms, discrepancy perfectionism, and order perfectionism.
